results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 53 aligned summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p51, with the declared section order oms before channels); the three callouts are apparatus (null). Changing a Placed Order ¶2 matches p19 in its summary, though its sentence 'After a warehouse accepts the work, cancellation becomes a request' names cancellation where p19 says the edit becomes a request (recorded under flow, B7).

results.quote: Four homes are possible: the three candidates above and a service the merchant builds itself. **1. The platform's order is the record.**
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases (four homes introduced; option 1 and its limit). p34's controlling idea is option 1 only; the four-homes announcement is a section lead-in fused into the option-1 paragraph (flow reader B, item 12, also stumbled on it). The fourth option was already announced in Many Channels ¶3, so the lead-in can be cut or reduced to a clause.

The other units marked two_ideas hold one controlling idea as the spec declares it: Introduction ¶2 (p02 is the thesis: one record, and the OMS as its home once two of four conditions hold), In Practice ¶1 (p41 includes the rollout and 'after which every order is created in the OMS'), In Practice ¶4 (p43 joins per-parcel summary and per-shipment invoice), Questions to Ask ¶2 (p51 is the recap-and-hand-off transition).

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene and record to S1/S2, state machines to S2, changes to S3, routing to S4, OMS/channels/choices/trade-offs/stages to S5, In Practice to S2/S5/S6, When It Goes Wrong to S6; introduction and conclusion units are apparatus or synthesis.

results.quote: Stripped to what every downstream system needs, the record has six parts.
results.finding: The six-part table is introduced but no sentence says what it shows (spec: each part has its own readers, so the record serves warehouse, finance, carrier, service and customer at once); the next unit moves straight to the cart/order/shipment/invoice distinctions.

All other evidence is explained: the scene's status table and Figure 1 ('Each system exposed a different part of the situation'); Shopify, fulfillment-order and commercetools sources and the four-machine table and Figure 2 (read by State Machines ¶5); the 'Delivered' table ('claims less than readers assume'); Adobe/Shopify routing rules ('know about stock and geography. They do not know...'); Kibo/Fluent/Manhattan quotations and Figure 3 ('worth reading as a specification', read by ¶4); OMS vendor quotations ('the vendors describe the same shape'); the OMS component table ('What the OMS owns, and what it leaves alone, is the point'); Figure 4; the candidates table and Fluent quotation ('three truths about the same order'); the €4,500 / €320,000 price; the trade-offs table (read by 'My judgement'); the stage table (read by ¶2); the requirements table and Figure 5 ('Only order creation and edits must be exact and immediate'); the webhook statistic ('The same recovery requirement applies to a smaller merchant'); the failure table (read by ¶2).

results.quote: Fluent Commerce states the boundary plainly on its own site: "your ERP stays the system of record" for finance, while the OMS decides where orders go and writes back (n.d., accessed November 2026).
results.finding: Declared: elaboration, sentence at the start of this unit, carrying over the three candidates and introducing that they are owners of different truths, not rivals. The unit opens on the Fluent quotation ('the boundary' with no antecedent) and only its second sentence ('The three records are not rivals') makes the elaboration; reorder so that sentence leads and the quotation supports it.

All other boundaries express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information: 'The merchant needs one record that brings those facts together' (problem_solution), 'Where we are in the order's journey' with the payment webhook (time), 'The chapter's case, though, is not Eva's order' (contrast), 'could not represent a partial shipment' (cause_effect), 'Meanwhile' (time), 'Eleven tickets followed' (cause_effect), 'made the remedy decision W2' (problem_solution), 'Three distinctions trip up newcomers' (contrast), 'The order number is the one thing every system ... share' (elaboration), 'Shopify keeps' (example), 'Below the order' (place), 'commercetools, a second platform, separates the same machines' (similarity), 'are summaries computed from the machines below' (cause_effect), 'Edits.' / 'Holds.' / 'Cancellations.' (sequence), 'Platforms route by simple rules' (example), 'the fuller decision' (contrast), 'The business trade-off inside a split' (cause_effect), 'a split in time rather than space' (similarity), 'What the OMS owns' (elaboration), 'When does that junction need' (cause_effect), 'The alternative to the junction' (problem_solution), '2.' '3.' '4.' (sequence), 'My judgement' (cause_effect), 'The shape of the record does not change with scale' (conclusion_summary), 'Under W2, each interaction' (elaboration), 'Replay #1052877 through that design' (example), 'The fleece's dispatch and delivery' (time), 'The customer still waits' (contrast), 'Most rows end the same way' (conclusion_summary), 'Go back to the opening's order', 'Established.' / 'Depends on context.' / 'The author's synthesis.', and the closing 'Under W2, an order like Eva's'.

Both readers describe the declared organisation: the opening failure case, then the record from the inside out (parts, number, state machines, changes, routing), then the system that holds it and the choice of home (prerequisite_order with problem_solution and comparison), then the design at work and its failures. ¶1 states what no section states alone: each fact behind 'Partially delivered: 1 of 2 parcels' is first known by a different system, so only one record that keeps the lines apart and is where every channel's order is created can say it, and the home follows from who answers the parcel question; the established / context / synthesis lists and the nine questions turn it into a course of action for the reader's company.

The intro-only reader predicted the sections in order (record and number, states and computed status, edits/holds/cancellations, routing, the OMS, when channels need one home and which system, four homes by trade-off and scale stage, the chosen design with #1052877 replayed, failures), the central Three-Status Order case, and the evidence (Kestrel & Pine case, platform and OMS vendor documentation), in an explanatory, practical tone.

Matches expected: 'Partially delivered: 1 of 2 parcels' and 'ships in two parcels', the summary taken from the least-advanced shipment; the design had one status word (no per-shipment goods state) and no single home owning the order across platform, WMS and ERP.

Matches expected: yes, two of the four conditions hold (two channels, two warehouses), so one system must be the order's home; an OMS rather than the ERP because the hub must route between warehouses and answer a parcel question, which a batch finance system cannot. The reader did not say explicitly 'not decided by revenue', but its answer rests only on the conditions, not on size.

Matches expected: a shipped order cannot be canceled; it becomes a return (label, receipt, inspection, refund on receipt), a compensation the order's home coordinates; edits and cancellations after warehouse acceptance become requests.
